window.basis: Cited: the Lancet Commission on Global Surgery's 2-hour access indicator (share of people within 2 hours of a facility that can do caesarean section, laparotomy and treatment of open fracture). Holmer et al. 2019, Br J Surg, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6790969, note that it "does not capture whether patients actually receive care".
window.note: Windows are planning thresholds for estimated free-flow drive time, not clinical deadlines: a facility just outside a window may still be the right place to go.

emoc.basis: Cited: the Lancet Commission on Global Surgery's 2-hour access indicator (share of people within 2 hours of a facility that can do caesarean section, laparotomy and treatment of open fracture). Holmer et al. 2019, Br J Surg, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6790969, note that it "does not capture whether patients actually receive care".

nicu.basis: Design choice: no published travel-time standard was found for this service; set equal to the 2-hour emergency indicator.

dialysis.basis: Design choice informed by DOPPS (Moist et al. 2008, Clin J Am Soc Nephrol): longer travel time to dialysis went with worse quality of life, adherence and survival. Dialysis is repeated two or three times a week, so the window is short. The 60 minutes is ours.

icu.basis: Design choice: no published travel-time standard was found for this service; set equal to the 2-hour emergency indicator.

cardiac_surgery.basis: Design choice: no published travel-time standard was found for this service; heart surgery is usually planned, so 4 hours.

cath_lab.basis: Design choice informed by ESC 2023, which sets "an absolute time of 120 min from STEMI diagnosis to PCI-mediated reperfusion" (https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/article/44/38/3720/7243210). The 90-minute travel window inside that is ours, not ESC's.

mri.basis: Design choice: no published travel-time standard was found for this service; MRI is usually planned, so 3 hours.

ct.basis: Design choice: no published travel-time standard was found for this service; set equal to the 2-hour emergency indicator.

trauma.basis: Cited: the Lancet Commission on Global Surgery's 2-hour access indicator (share of people within 2 hours of a facility that can do caesarean section, laparotomy and treatment of open fracture). Holmer et al. 2019, Br J Surg, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6790969, note that it "does not capture whether patients actually receive care".

burns.basis: Design choice: no published travel-time standard was found for this service; specialist burn units are few, so 4 hours.

neurosurgery.basis: Design choice informed by Seelig et al. 1981 (N Engl J Med): comatose patients with an acute subdural haematoma did much better when operated within 4 hours of injury. The 2.5-hour travel window is ours.

oncology.basis: Design choice: no published travel-time standard was found for this service; cancer treatment is planned and repeated, so 4 hours.

travel_model.text: Estimated drive time = state terrain factor x 2.30 x km^0.842 minutes, from the straight-line km. Fitted to 934 free-flow car trips (OSRM) from 30 post offices. Error: leave-one-anchor-out log SD 0.26; the shown range (x e^-0.52 to x e^+0.52) held 94.6% of held-out trips. The factor is the origin state's (reference/terrain_multiplier.csv). Free-flow means no traffic and no waiting: real trips take longer. Islands: sea travel is not modelled, so no minutes are shown there.

recipe: Claimed: lists obstetrics or maternity care, or mentions deliveries or a labour ward.
Supported: a fact names caesarean section (C-section, LSCS).
Corroborated: caesarean section, a blood bank or transfusion, and anaesthesia or an operating theatre are all named.
Based on the WHO signal functions for comprehensive emergency obstetric care, which add caesarean section and blood transfusion to basic care.
how_we_decided.grades_status: recipe v0.2 from bundle grades.parquet: the v0.3 grades the v1-final spec gates on (D048) were not found, so the older rules are used. Rebuild with scripts/wp3_regrade_v03.py and scripts/wp12_bundle.py.
how_we_decided.tagger: Evidence tags: the shipped tagger scores macro F1 0.91 (95% interval 0.90 to 0.93) on 777 agent-labelled gold facts; weakest tag neurosurgery at 0.58.

gates.rule: the facility has a location we can use
claims the service and is within about 6 h estimated drive (3 x the window), the search limit for the further-away line
grade 2 or 3 under recipe v0.2 (a fact in the record names the service) and no major warning for this service
estimated drive time within the 120-minute window (cited; about 108 km straight-line from here at terrain factor 1.01 (Uttar Pradesh))

how_we_decided.formula: Nearest first by estimated drive time. One declared evidence allowance: a corroborated record can be listed before a nearer supported one if it is at most 15 minutes further. Equal times are ties, listed by straight-line km. Trust, page dates, web domains and warnings are shown on the card; they do not reorder it.
how_we_decided.order_rule: Nearest first by estimated drive time. One declared evidence allowance: a corroborated record can be listed before a nearer supported one if it is at most 15 minutes further. Equal times are ties, listed by straight-line km. Trust, page dates, web domains and warnings are shown on the card; they do not reorder it.
how_we_decided.tie_rule: Equal estimated minutes are ties, listed by straight-line km; never by warnings.
how_we_decided.probability: Nothing here is a probability. Grades say what the facility's own web record names, the drive times are estimates from straight-line distance, and the windows and the allowance are declared thresholds.
limits: Drive times are estimates from straight-line distance, free-flow (no traffic, no waiting). Real trips take longer.
Windows are planning thresholds, not clinical deadlines.
The data is a sample of mostly private, web-visible facilities. Public hospitals are under-covered, so no result often means not in this data.
Grades describe what web pages say, not what a facility can do today. Pages can be stale.
Citations name the fact and its field, not the web page it came from: the data has no per-fact source.
